# LB1 / 1st Place — Score-improvement tricks

> Evidence cites `../writeup/lb1-writeup.md` (= `temp/LB1.pdf`) unless noted. "reusable by us" judged against our repo state (notes.md / equation-frontier.md / submissions.md).
> Impact labels are the author's qualitative attribution, not isolated ablations (the team rarely ran clean ablations; LB had high variance).

| trick | description | evidence / source | likely impact | reusable by us? | implementation difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Signature catalog (cryptarithm)** | Exhaustively enumerate 100×100 operands × 22 non-join rules → 4,205 unique signatures; each maps to candidate rows (rule + slot digit string + candidate count). Model **memorizes** the catalog. | writeup §Cryptarithm: "4205 unique signatures", "ABCCCDD rows 15" | **High** — took cryptarithm path to Public 0.89 / Private 0.908 | **Yes — top priority.** We synth cryptarithm but have no memorizable catalog. | High (enumerate + normalize + render into traces) |
| **Candidate-count memorization + anchor selection** | The memorized per-signature candidate count picks the DFS anchor (smallest count) and search order; `sig8` rule lets length-8 signatures fix multiplication early if count ≤ max(30, 2·min). | writeup §Cryptarithm "4 Candidate rows" | **High** (part of the above lever) | **Yes** — pairs with signature catalog | Medium |
| **DFS with Observation-1/2 pruning** | Same 24-rule inventory; Obs.1 = all non-join ops share one mode (normal/flip); Obs.2 = non-join ops don't reuse a group. Prunes branches without search. | writeup §Equation/Cryptarithm "Observation 1/2" | **Medium-High** | **Yes** — cheap, structural | Medium |
| **HEX compression of bit columns** | Nemotron tokenizer ≈ 1 token/bit-char; convert bit strings length ≥4 to hex. **Median gen tokens 6771 → 4888 (−27.8%)**, freeing budget. | writeup §Bit "median ... 6771 to 4888 (27.8% reduction)" | **High** (enabler) | **Yes — cheap, high ROI.** We never compressed traces. | Low |
| **Rule-sequence catalog + Hamming repair (bit)** | Enumerate all valid 8-bit transforms → normalize to 8-rule sequences → 5,238 valid; at inference retrieve ≤32 nearest (Hamming over 8 rule slots) and apply first that matches all 8 output bits. Rejects non-catalog seqs (e.g. `default 1`). | writeup §Bit "5238 valid 8-rule sequences", "up to 32 catalog candidates" | **High** — repair + extra training → Public 0.91 / Private 0.920 | **Yes** — medium effort | Medium-High |
| **Extra bit rule families** | majority, par3, ch, sel_nand_xnor, ao/oa/ax/ox/xa/xo; chosen to keep set compact (add/remove while preserving train coverage). | writeup §Bit rule table | **Medium** | **Yes** — extends our bounded solver (currently ~10% bit coverage) | Medium |
| **Repair-format "fix only the final answer"** | A teacher trace whose CoT is solver-derived but whose `\boxed{}` is the ground truth taught the model to *correct* a wrong solver at the last step. (Discovered accidentally.) | writeup §Bit "accidental inconsistent trace" | **Medium** | **Maybe** — risky (teaches non-faithful traces); test carefully | Low (but subtle) |
| **24-rule inventory (equation numeric)** | All operator transforms over `AB op CD` explained by 24 rules across join/add/sub/mul × normal/flip. | writeup §Equation "24-rule inventory" table | **Medium** | **Yes — but re-check premise.** Contradicts our EQ "global cipher" verdict for the *deduce* subset. | Medium |
| **Operator priors (+, −, *)** | Bias `+`→add-like, `*`→mul-like to break ties; used in equation numeric, **NOT** transferred to cryptarithm. | writeup §Equation "operator priors" | **Low-Medium** | **Yes** (equation only) | Low |
| **Guess-category handling** | equation guess: infer mode/groups from other operators + priors + train frequency. cryptarithm guess: write an early `join` candidate to `\boxed{}`, then replace if the full search resolves. | writeup Q&A | **Low-Medium** (long tail) | **Yes** | Low |
| **77-word plaintext vocabulary (cipher)** | Constrain unknown-word decoding to the 77 plaintext words in train.csv. | writeup §Text Cipher | **Low** (cipher already ~100% solver) | **Yes** — strengthens our cipher solver | Low |
| **Continuation training (bit-weighted, low LR)** | After main SFT, continue on bit-heavy extra data at LR 1e-5 for 6,500 steps. | writeup §Synthetic Data / SFT | **Medium** | **Partly** — needs sustained GPU (we have RTX Pro 6000 post-comp only) | Medium (compute-bound) |
| **lm_head in LoRA targets** | Included but a commenter notes vLLM ignores `lm_head` at inference → likely no effect. | writeup Q&A | **~Zero** | Skip | n/a |
| **Massive single-GPU SFT (>1B tokens)** | 119h main + 51h extra on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell. | writeup §Compute | **High** (enabler) but infra-bound | **No** during a live comp (Kaggle ≤8h kernels); partial post-comp | High (compute) |

## Notes on attribution / provenance
- **Built on @huikang** (Open Progress Prize): the per-output-bit bit solver and the join/join_swap + backtracking cryptarithm DFS. Confirmed in `github.com/tonghuikang/nemotron` (`reasoners/bit_manipulation.py`, `investigators/cryptarithm_deduce.py`). See `../source_index.md`.
- **Signature viewpoint** credited to **@youkinasa** ("A Pattern-Matching Approach to Solving Symbolic Arithmetic Puzzles"); LB1's increment = turning the lookup table into a *memorized* catalog (no eval-time program allowed).
- **@kemshim** ("Trying to improve cryptarithm") independently explored memorizing a mul pattern table near comp end; thread with @MAJ0RT0M discussed learnability limits.
- HEX compression, signature catalog, rule-sequence catalog + Hamming repair, candidate-count memorization are **novel to LB1** (absent from @huikang's public code).
